summary: The brief step (own-dashboard/src/lib/marketing/dneskai-briefs.ts, 496 lines, no model) turns each selected event into a dneskai-brief/1 with evidence ranked publisher > newsroom > aggregator, at most 20 pictures, a suggested format and one of four fixed Prague slots, then admits it as a guarded generation job only when a verified @dneskai Instagram account exists. The owner brief's map is accurate except for one line number (:112 is :111) and the lapse wording (the day's last brief lapses as brief-target-date-passed; brief-expired cannot fire first). The biggest problems are upstream of the model: evidence is the feed description capped at 2,000 chars (RSS content:encoded and the fetched article body are both discarded), the 400-char/one-picture rule locks generation into single-image posts, a held brief that lapses leaves its candidates `selected` so the event can never be re-selected for 30 days, generation is gated on the publishing account although only the publisher needs it, and the owner has no path to re-slot, retry, release or generate anyway. Nothing in the brief carries a hook or kit hint. Measured: 36/42 tests pass locally and the 6 failures are a machine-timezone leak in the dry-day test (9/9 pass with TZ=UTC).

findings.title: Feed-description evidence plus the 400-char/one-picture rule lock most briefs into single-image posts, and generation cannot upgrade them
